dictionary-lang.markdownDescription:
This special property is used by dictionaries. Add it only if you're using the 'dictionary' attribute.
Example: dictionary-lang: "en"

loots.markdownDescription: Create loots (item drop) based on broken block, killed entity and on fishing

scripts.markdownDescription:
Scripts that run custom code on specific events.
For now they can be executed on items and custom entities.

blocks_populators.markdownDescription:
Create rules to spawn custom ores around your worlds.
**They will be spawned only on new chunks.**
**Pregenerated worlds or already generated chunks won't be affected to avoid risky overwrite**

trees_populators.markdownDescription:
Create rules to spawn custom trees around your worlds.
**They will be spawned only on new chunks.**
**Pregenerated worlds or already generated chunks won't be affected to avoid risky overwrite**

surface_decorators.markdownDescription:
Create rules to spawn custom blocks on the surface of your worlds.
**They will be spawned only on new chunks.**
**Pregenerated worlds or already generated chunks won't be affected to avoid risky overwrite**

cave_decorators.markdownDescription:
Create rules to spawn custom blocks in the caves of your worlds.
**They will be spawned only on new chunks.**
**Pregenerated worlds or already generated chunks won't be affected to avoid risky overwrite**

entities_populators.markdownDescription: Create rules to spawn custom entities around your worlds.

font_images.markdownDescription:
Create your own font characters. You can use them as emoji, GUI texture, HUD...
It's basically an image shown in texts.

huds.markdownDescription: Create your own HUDs. You will be able to show mana on screen, fuel, current minigame level, heat and anything you want to add!

categories.markdownDescription: Create your own categories and show them in /ia command

minecraft_lang_overwrite.markdownDescription: Replace language attributes to your custom value.

dictionary.markdownDescription:
Create a special list of texts to be used (almost) anywhere and get translated automatically by the plugin.
For example: in items names, lores, /ia menu categories names

additionalProperties.markdownDescription: You can then use this property name as any item name or /ia category, it will be replaced with this value.

display-category-example-category-name.markdownDescription: You can then use this property name as any item name or /ia category, it will be replaced with this value.

my_display-name-.markdownDescription: You can then use this property name as any item name or /ia category, it will be replaced with this value.

entities.markdownDescription: Create a custom entity with 3D model

armors_rendering.markdownDescription: (**OLD NAME**, use the new `legacy_armor_renderings` instead) Create legacy custom armors rendering which use shaders to show custom textures.

legacy_armor_renderings.markdownDescription: Create legacy custom armors rendering which use shaders to show custom textures.

attribute_modifiers.markdownDescription: These are the vanilla attribute modifiers, you can get more info here https://minecraft.gamepedia.com/Attribute#Attributes_available_on_all_living_entities

attribute_modifier.markdownDescription:
You can directly set a value or set `value` and `operation`.
## Examples:
```
attribute_modifiers:
  mainhand:
    attackDamage: 2
```
Or:
```
attribute_modifiers:
  mainhand:
    attackDamage:
      value: 2
      operation: add
```

anyOf.markdownDescription:
You can directly set a value or set `value` and `operation`.
## Examples:
```
attribute_modifiers:
  mainhand:
    attackDamage: 2
```
Or:
```
attribute_modifiers:
  mainhand:
    attackDamage:
      value: 2
      operation: add
```

custom_potion_effect.description: Attach a specific potion effect to this potion.

colors.markdownDescription:
Valid colors can be obtained from here: https://hub.spigotmc.org/javadocs/bukkit/org/bukkit/Color.html
If you want very precise color you can use this website to get the Decimal value: https://www.mathsisfun.com/hexadecimal-decimal-colors.html

results.markdownDescription: List of the possible result drops and their chances

armor.markdownDescription:
Old way of creating custom armors. For Minecraft 1.21.1 and lower.

If your server accepts 1.21.2 and higher, use the `custom_armor` property instead.

custom_armor.markdownDescription:
Specify a name from previously created 'armors_rendering' textures for this armor piece.
Read more: https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/advanced/custom-armors/

If you decide to specify 'custom_armor' you can avoid setting the 'color' property here.

effects.description: Attach multiple potion effects to this potion to create a completely custom potion.

can_be_recolored_in_crafting_table.markdownDescription: Can be recolored by putting it into the crafting table with a dye item (vanilla behaviour for dyeable items).

enabled.markdownDescription:
With this setting you can disable an item completely.
**Obviously if a player has it in inventory it won't be removed, he still will own it.
Same thing for blocks, but when broken they won't drop anymore**

template.markdownDescription:
Templates are special items that won't appear ingame, they are used as properties holders for other items.
They allow you to write common properties in one item and add them automatically to other items without constant copy and paste.

https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/advanced/item-properties/basic/templates-and-variants

This is useful to create items with the same logic but different texture/model, name, lore (for example I use it to create a furniture with different woods without having to copy and paste the "furniture" behaviour everytime).

variant_of.markdownDescription:
Name of the template you want to use.
Variants are items that will appear ingame and will inherit properties of template items.

https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/advanced/item-properties/basic/templates-and-variants

This is useful to create items with the same logic but different texture/model, name, lore (for example I use it to create a furniture with different woods without having to copy and paste the "furniture" behaviour everytime).

display_name.markdownDescription:
(**OLD NAME**, use `name` instead). Display name of the item.
You can set a **text** or an identifier from a **dictionary** file.

Get more info about translations here: https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/languages

name.markdownDescription:
Item name.
You can set a **text** or an identifier from a **dictionary** file.

Get more info about translations here: https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/languages

permission_suffix.markdownDescription:
Partial permission of the item.

For example `iasurvival.ruby_block` is a suffix permission for `ia.user.ia.seeitem.iasurvival.ruby_block` and might be extended in the future for new plugin permissions.

mmoitem.markdownDescription: Special property to mark item as MMOITEM https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/39267/

use_mmoitem_displayname.markdownDescription: Use the display name of MMOitems item instead of the one from ItemsAdder. Default `false`.

resource.markdownDescription:
(Old way of creating the item graphics. Use `graphics` property on 1.21.4+ instead.) Resource pack model generator settings.
`material` property is required for every item.
However custom armors do not require this setting.
Custom armors default item material will be leather if not specified.

generate.markdownDescription:
`true` to automatically generate the JSON model from your textures.

`false` to create the model by yourself.

Set to `true` if you want to use `textures`.
Set `false` if you want to use `model_path`.

model_path.markdownDescription:
Path to the model file.

Example: `item/my_item`, `my_items:item/my_item` or `minecraft:item/diamond`.

icon.title:
(1.21.4+ clients only!) Texture to be shown in inventory instead of the item model.
Example: `item/my_item_icon`, `my_items:item/my_item_icon` or `minecraft:item/diamond`.

generate.markdownDescription:
`true` to automatically generate the JSON model from your textures.

`false` to create the model by yourself.

Set to `true` if you want to use `textures`.
Set `false` if you want to use `model_path`.

custom_model_data.markdownDescription:
(optional) Force the usage of a defined `custom_model_data` (`CustomModelData`).
https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/item-properties/resource#manually-specify-custom_model_data

model_id.markdownDescription:
(**OLD NAME**, use `custom_model_data` instead). If you want to force the usage of a defined `custom_model_data` (CustomModelData) you can set this value.
https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/item-properties/resource#manually-specify-custom_model_data

textures.title: Set `generate: true` to use this!
textures.markdownDescription:
Specifies the textures layers to be used to generate the model. You usually will need only 1 layer.
If you are creating a block you can set a texture for each face of the block in this order:
- block/block_down.png
- block/block_east.png
- block/block_north.png
- block/block_south.png
- block/block_up.png
- block/block_west.png

texture.title: Set `generate: true` to use this!
texture.markdownDescription:
Specifies the texture layer to be used to generate the model.
If you are creating a block you can set a texture for each face of the block in this order:
- block/block_down.png
- block/block_east.png
- block/block_north.png
- block/block_south.png
- block/block_up.png
- block/block_west.png

parent.markdownDescription:
(optional) Parent model of the item.

This is useful to create items that are based on other items.
This option is generally used by advanced resourcepacks artists.

Example: `item/my_item_icon`, `my_items:item/my_item_icon` or `minecraft:item/diamond`.

`false` to create the model by yourself.

Set to `true` if you want to use `textures`.
Set `false` if you want to use `model_path`.

(optional) Force the usage of a defined `custom_model_data` (`CustomModelData`).
https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/item-properties/resource#manually-specify-custom_model_data

https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/item-properties/resource#manually-specify-custom_model_data

Path to the model file.

Example: `item/my_item`, `my_items:item/my_item` or `minecraft:item/diamond`.

icon.title:
(1.21.4+ clients only!) Texture to be shown in inventory instead of the item model.
Example: `item/my_item_icon`, `my_items:item/my_item_icon` or `minecraft:item/diamond`.

material.markdownDescription:
(Default `PAPER`) Material of the item.
You can use any vanilla material or a custom item created in ItemsAdder.

item_model.markdownDescription:
Manually handling the item model on your own using the new 1.21.4 format. (Refer to the online tutorial about that. This is not a normal json model).
Example: `test:modern_item` which is inside `contents/test/items/modern_item.json`.

graphics.markdownDescription: Decide how the item is shown in-game

hand_animation_on_swap.markdownDescription: (default `true`) Whether to play the hand swap animation when switching to this item.

parent.markdownDescription:
(optional) Parent model of the item.

This is useful to create items that are based on other items.
This option is generally used by advanced resourcepacks artists.

Example: `block/cross`, `item/handheld`...

icon.markdownDescription:
(1.21.4+ clients only!) Texture to be shown in inventory instead of the item model.
Example: `item/my_item_icon`, `my_items:item/my_item_icon` or `minecraft:item/diamond`.

color.markdownDescription: (Optional) Color of the tintindex 0 of the model. Read more [here](https://github.com/PluginBugs/Issues-ItemsAdder/issues/4945#issuecomment-3228170950).

color2.markdownDescription: (Optional) Color of the tintindex 1 of the model. Read more [here](https://github.com/PluginBugs/Issues-ItemsAdder/issues/4945#issuecomment-3228170950)

texture.markdownDescription:
Specifies the texture layer to be used to generate the model.
If you are creating a block the texture will be applied to all faces of the block.

model.markdownDescription:
Location of the model file.

Example: `item/my_item`, `my_items:item/my_item` or `minecraft:item/diamond`.

textures.markdownDescription:
Specifies the textures layers to be used to generate the model. You usually will need only 1 layer.
If you are creating a block you can set a texture for each face of the block. Refer to the wiki. If not specified, the `texture` property will be used.

normal.markdownDescription: Texture for the normal state of the item. Required for bundles and used for an empty bundle. **Bundle graphics require ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.**

filled.markdownDescription: **Requires ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.** Optional texture for a non-empty bundle, used when `minecraft:bundle/fullness` is greater than zero. Falls back to `normal`.

open_back.markdownDescription: **Requires ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.** Optional back layer of an open bundle. Shown only in a GUI when `minecraft:bundle/has_selected_item` is true. ItemsAdder generates its model with `minecraft:item/template_bundle_open_back` and renders it before `minecraft:bundle/selected_item` and `open_front`.

open_front.markdownDescription: **Requires ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.** Optional front layer of an open bundle. Shown only in a GUI when `minecraft:bundle/has_selected_item` is true. ItemsAdder generates its model with `minecraft:item/template_bundle_open_front` and renders it after `open_back` and `minecraft:bundle/selected_item`.

north.markdownDescription: Texture for the north face of the block.

south.markdownDescription: Texture for the south face of the block.

east.markdownDescription: Texture for the east face of the block.

west.markdownDescription: Texture for the west face of the block.

up.markdownDescription: Texture for the up face of the block.

down.markdownDescription: Texture for the down face of the block.

pulling_0.markdownDescription: Texture for the pulling_0 state of the item (for bows and crossbows). You can use any pulling stage, for example pulling_1, pulling_2, pulling_3...

pulling_1.markdownDescription: Texture for the pulling_0 state of the item (for bows and crossbows). You can use any pulling stage, for example pulling_1, pulling_2, pulling_3...

pulling_2.markdownDescription: Texture for the pulling_0 state of the item (for bows and crossbows). You can use any pulling stage, for example pulling_1, pulling_2, pulling_3...

cast.markdownDescription: Texture for the cast state of the item (for fishing rods).

rocket.markdownDescription: Texture for the rocket state of the item (for crossbow loaded a firework).

arrow.markdownDescription: Texture for the arrow state of the item (for crossbow loaded an arrow).

throwing.markdownDescription: Texture for the throwing state of the item (for tridents).

blocking.markdownDescription: Texture for the blocking state of the item (for shields).

models.markdownDescription:
Locations of the models to be used for different item states.
If a state is not specified, the `model` property will be used.

normal.markdownDescription: Model for the normal state of the item. Used for an empty bundle. **Bundle graphics require ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.**

filled.markdownDescription: **Requires ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.** Optional model for a non-empty bundle, used when `minecraft:bundle/fullness` is greater than zero. Falls back to `normal`.

open_back.markdownDescription: **Requires ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.** Optional back model layer of an open bundle. Shown only in a GUI when `minecraft:bundle/has_selected_item` is true, before `minecraft:bundle/selected_item` and `open_front`.

open_front.markdownDescription: **Requires ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.** Optional front model layer of an open bundle. Shown only in a GUI when `minecraft:bundle/has_selected_item` is true, after `open_back` and `minecraft:bundle/selected_item`.

pulling_0.markdownDescription: Model for the pulling_0 state of the item (for bows and crossbows). You can use any pulling stage, for example pulling_1, pulling_2, pulling_3...

pulling_1.markdownDescription: Model for the pulling_0 state of the item (for bows and crossbows). You can use any pulling stage, for example pulling_1, pulling_2, pulling_3...

pulling_2.markdownDescription: Model for the pulling_0 state of the item (for bows and crossbows). You can use any pulling stage, for example pulling_1, pulling_2, pulling_3...

cast.markdownDescription: Model for the cast state of the item (for fishing rods).

rocket.markdownDescription: Model for the rocket state of the item (for crossbow loaded a firework).

arrow.markdownDescription: Model for the arrow state of the item (for crossbow loaded an arrow).

throwing.markdownDescription: Model for the throwing state of the item (for tridents).

blocking.markdownDescription: Model for the blocking state of the item (for shields).

attribute_modifiers.markdownDescription: Slot in which the item has effect

max_custom_durability.markdownDescription:
(**OLD NAME**, please use `max_durability`).
Max durability of the item. If not specified ItemsAdder will use default material max durability

custom_durability.markdownDescription:
(**OLD NAME**, please use `durability`).
Current durability of the item (when crafted or obtained with command).
If not specified ItemsAdder will use material max durability (undamaged)

max_durability.markdownDescription: Max durability of the item. If not specified ItemsAdder will use default material max durability

durability.markdownDescription:
Current durability of the item (when crafted or obtained with command).
If not specified ItemsAdder will use material max durability (undamaged)

disappear_when_broken.markdownDescription: If the item should disappear when broken

unbreakable.markdownDescription: If the item can get damage

repair_cost.markdownDescription: Initial cost to repair the item in an anvil

usages.markdownDescription: Usages of the item before it disappears (you must handle usages using an event and action (decrement_usages) https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/item-properties/events/actions

item_flags.markdownDescription:
Vanilla Minecraft item flags.
Special item flags that can hide some vanilla info of the item.
You can find a detailed info list here: https://hub.spigotmc.org/javadocs/spigot/org/bukkit/inventory/ItemFlag.html

max_stack_size.markdownDescription: Max stack size of the item

enabled.markdownDescription:
(default `true`) If the item should be automatically updated when the resource pack is updated.

If set to `false` you will need to use the `/iaitem update` command to update the item.

fix_unstackable_items_on_click.markdownDescription: (default `true`) On click, force merging of items if they are similar but `name`, `item_name`, `lore` and some more are different, but `namespace` and `id` are the same. Note: this will be ignored if the global setting in config.yml is `false`.

consumable.markdownDescription:
## Available on `1.21.2+` clients/servers only!
Consumable item. Can be eaten or drank or used in a general way if no food properties are set.

nutrition.markdownDescription: Nutrition value of the food item. Not mandatory.

saturation.markdownDescription: Saturation value of the food item. Not mandatory.

can_always_eat.markdownDescription: If the player can eat the food item even if they are not hungry. Not mandatory.

consume_seconds.markdownDescription: How many seconds it takes to consume the food item.

sound.markdownDescription: Sound of the food item when eaten. Available on `1.21.2+` clients only!

particles.markdownDescription: If the particles of the food item should be shown. Available on `1.21.2+` clients only!

animation.markdownDescription: Animation of the food item when eaten. Available on `1.21.2+` clients only!

effects.markdownDescription: Effects of the consumable item when consumed

elytra.markdownDescription:
## Requires Minecraft `1.21.2+` and ItemsAdder `4.0.18+`!
Configures this item as a custom Elytra. ItemsAdder automatically creates the required chest equipment, enables gliding and generates the wings equipment model.

wings_texture.markdownDescription: Texture rendered as wings while this Elytra is equipped. The path is relative to the namespace's `textures` folder. Recommended size: `64x32` or another `2:1` resolution. Example: `entity/equipment/wings/sky_elytra`.

broken_item_texture.markdownDescription: Optional inventory and hand texture used when the Elytra is broken. If omitted, ItemsAdder looks for `<graphics.texture>_broken`. This does not change the equipped wings texture. Example: `item/sky_elytra_broken`.

max_flight_ticks.markdownDescription: Maximum continuous gliding time in ticks. `0` means unlimited. There are 20 ticks in one second.

firework.markdownDescription: Controls firework boosts while gliding with this custom Elytra.

enabled.markdownDescription: Whether fireworks can boost the player while using this Elytra.

consume.markdownDescription: Whether an accepted boost consumes the firework rocket.

cooldown_ticks.markdownDescription: Required delay in ticks between accepted firework boosts.

durability_damage_multiplier.markdownDescription: Multiplier applied to durability damage. `0` disables durability damage for this Elytra.

collision_damage_multiplier.markdownDescription: Multiplier applied to `FLY_INTO_WALL` damage. `0` disables wall-collision damage for this Elytra.

equipment.markdownDescription:
## Available on `1.21.2+` clients/servers only!
If present, this item can be equipped by players in the selected slot.

id.markdownDescription: Equipment ID. Must be a valid ID of an equipment created under the `equipments` section.

legacy_armor_rendering_id.markdownDescription: Legacy armor rendering ID. Must be a valid ID of a legacy armor rendering created under the `legacy_armor_renderings` section.

slot.markdownDescription:
Slot in which this item can be equipped. This is automatically set if the item is a vanilla armor piece.
Example: `material: IRON_HELMET` will automatically set `slot: HEAD`.

camera_overlay_id.markdownDescription: (optional): namespaced ID of the overlay texture to use when equipped. Example: `minecraft:misc/pumpkinblur` (which addresses `assets/minecraft/textures/misc/pumpkinblur.png`).

sound.markdownDescription: (optional): sound to play when equipped. Example: `minecraft:item.armor.equip_iron`.

dispensable.markdownDescription: (default: `true`), whether the item can be equipped by using a Dispenser.

swappable.markdownDescription: boolean (default: `true`), whether the item can be equipped into the relevant slot by right-clicking.

allowed_entities.markdownDescription:
(optional): Entity ID, Entity Tag, or list of Entity IDs to limit which entities can equip this item
If not specified, any entity (that can wear this kind of equipment) is allowed to equip this item

damage_on_hurt.markdownDescription: (default: `true`), whether this item will be damaged when the wearing entity is damaged.

slot_attribute_modifiers.markdownDescription: (optional) Attribute modifiers to be applied when equipped on the previously specified `slot`.

glider.markdownDescription: (default: `false`), whether this item can be used to glide (without the Elytra).

tooltip_style.markdownDescription:
## Available on `1.21.2+` clients/servers only!
Namespaced ID for a tooltip style. If present, this item can use custom sprites for its tooltip background and frame.
`<namespace>:tooltip/<path>_background` and `<namespace>:tooltip/<path>_frame`.
## Example:
`my_items:tooltip/red` requires `my_items/textures/tooltip/red_frame.png` and `my_items/textures/tooltip/red_background.png`.

fire_resistant.markdownDescription: If the item is fire resistant, like nethgerite items.

hide_tooltip.markdownDescription: If the item tooltip should be hidden.

glint.markdownDescription:
Overrides the enchantment glint effect on an item.
If `true`, an item without an enchantment glint will display a glint.
If `false`, an item with a glint will not display this glint (either from enchantments or intrinsic properties of the item).

enchantment_glint_override.markdownDescription:
(**OLD NAME**, use `glint` instead). Overrides the enchantment glint effect on an item.
If `true`, an item without an enchantment glint will display a glint.
If `false`, an item with a glint will not display this glint (either from enchantments or intrinsic properties of the item).

enchants.markdownDescription:
Set default enchants to this item.
https://hub.spigotmc.org/javadocs/spigot/org/bukkit/enchantments/Enchantment.html

You can set also the enchant level, for example: 
- DIG_SPEED:5

You can also set other plugins enchants (if they provide your the ID), for example:- my_custom_plugin:custom_enchant:6
- blast_mining:1

blocked_enchants.markdownDescription:
Special item property that disables enchants for this item, so your users won't be able to enchant it.
https://hub.spigotmc.org/javadocs/spigot/org/bukkit/enchantments/Enchantment.html

nbt.markdownDescription:
(**OLD NAME**, use `components_nbt_file` instead).
Custom NBT properties for this custom item. Read here for more information: https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/advanced/custom-nbt

components_nbt_file.markdownDescription:
Path for the custom NBT properties file for this custom item.
Example: `my_item_nbt.json`.
Read here for more information: https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/advanced/custom-nbt

drop.markdownDescription: Customize some aspects of how the dropped item appears.

show_name.markdownDescription:
You can make a drop show its name.
Very useful for rare items.

glow.markdownDescription:
You can make an item glowing when dropped on the ground.
Very useful for rare items.

jukebox_disc.markdownDescription:
## Available on `1.21.1+` clients/servers only!
Use the item as a music disc. Replacement for the old `music_disc` behaviour.

song.markdownDescription:
Namespaced ID of the song to be played when this disc is inserted into a jukebox.
Example: `my_items:music/awesome_song`.

The song must be declared in the `sounds` section.

events_cooldown.markdownDescription:
(**OLD NAME** OF THE property `events_settings.cooldown.ticks`.

Use it instead.)

ticks.markdownDescription: Cooldown in ticks before user can activate events of this item

indicator.markdownDescription: Type of cooldown indicator, for now there is only HIDDEN and TITLE

custom_hud.markdownDescription: Namespaced ID if the custom hud used for this cooldown. Default value `_iainternal:small_cooldown_bar`.

all_actions_permission.markdownDescription:
Permission needed to execute any of the actions of each event.
If you want to set a different permission to eachaction you can add the 'permission' attribute on each action instead.

click_in_ia_gui.markdownDescription: If the item can be clicked in the ItemsAdder `/ia` GUI or if it does nothing on click.

permission.markdownDescription:
**OLD NAME** OF THE property `permission_suffix`.

Use `permission_suffix` instead.

name.markdownDescription:
Display name of the category.
You can set a **text** or an identifier from a **dictionary** file.

Get more info about dictionaries here: https://itemsadder.devs.beer/plugin-usage/adding-content/translation

title.markdownDescription: Display name of the category, inside the category view itself. Value of 'name' attribute will be used if not specified.

permission.markdownDescription: (**OLD NAME**, use the new `permission_suffix` instead, and do not include the complete permission.). Complete permission of the category. For example: `ia.menu.seecategory.special_items.group_1`.

permission_suffix.markdownDescription:
Partial permission used to allow a player to see the category.

For example `special_items.group_1` is a suffix permission for `ia.menu.seecategory.special_items.group_1`.

skip_if_already.markdownDescription: Skip this category if ItemsAdder already registered one with the same name from another .yml file

icon.markdownDescription: Icon of this category. Can be a custom item or a vanilla material

font_image.markdownDescription: Font image to be used as background of the category. Usually used for custom categories.

name.markdownDescription: Namespaced ID of the font_image to be used as background. (example: 'mcguis:blank_menu')

x_position_pixels.markdownDescription: Shift the font_image of some pixels on the X axis. Usually set to -16

title_position_pixels.markdownDescription: Shift the title text of some pixels on the X axis. Usually set to 0

show_all_items.markdownDescription: Show all items in this category (you can exclude some items using the hide_items attribute)

hide_items.markdownDescription: List of items to be hidden from this category (useful if you're using show_all_items property)

minecraft_lang_overwrite.markdownDescription: Easily customize entries in the Minecraft languages files.

languages.markdownDescription:
All the languages where you want to change these text in.

You should set it to only the languages of your playerbase to avoid useless resourcepack size increase. Set to `ALL` to support every user possible language.

anyOf.markdownDescription: Set to `ALL` to support every user possible language. No need to add other languages in this list.

type.markdownDescription:
**ENTITY requires ItemsAdder 4.0.18+.**

(USE THE MOUSE SCROLL WHELL for more..)
This property can have these value:

**REAL_WIRE**
uses a real block (tripwire), no lag, no entities, 100% real blocks.
downside: Max of 127 blocks in total.

**REAL_TRANSPARENT**
uses a real block (chorus), no lag, no entities, 100% real blocks, also with transparency support!
downside: max of 63 blocks in total

**TILE**
uses tile blocks (modified spawner with custom skin). It's not an entity but it have some downsides. Good thing is that you can create infinite blocks, there is no amount limit like REAL blocks.
downsides:
not a 100% real block, it's a retextured spawner
texture/model vanishes on high distance, so it will reveal the spawner vanilla texture
it could cause clientside lag if A LOT of blocks are in the player field of view, but only on lowend PCs.

**REAL_NOTE**
uses a real block (note_block), no lag, no entities, 100% real blocks.
downside: no support for transparency. Max of 750 blocks in total.
**REAL**
uses a real block (mushroom), no lag, no entities, 100% real blocks.
downside: max of 191 blocks in total

**FIRE**
this is a special type of block, it's the fire block.
downside: only a max of 14 custom fires is possible, so be sure to create only the ones you need.
